Claim 2: L1b, L2a and L6a compare the learner with fixed rules whose calibration labels are charged to the same budget, so the baseline has no free labels. L2a ratios are 1.050 to 1.139 with split-cluster CIs above 1. L6a ratios are 1.060 to 1.129 with CIs above 1. L7b agrees. This is a controlled comparison, so W2 is false. It is limited to some budgets: the learner loses at 10%. Claim 3: E04 is a different proxy (answer-only judge) with embedding delta AUC about -0.0003 and neighbor ratio 1.00. L1a on rollout-level proxies gives PC delta below 0.01 and ts/greedy at most 1.013. Both are non-E01 and below the thresholds, so claim 3 is killed and W3 is false.

Claim 3: E04 (different proxy, judge) has embedding delta AUC -0.0003 and neighbor ratio 1.00, confirmed in runs/E04/result.json (−0.0027 on 0.5B rung, ratios ~1.0). L1a and L11b also stay below 0.05. Nothing reaches 0.05 or 1.5, so killed. Claim 2: the free-label confound is controlled by charged, budget-matched baselines with no information advantage. L2a, L6a and L7b show the learner ahead with CI lower bounds above 1. L13a gives the same labels to both arms and still shows a gain, with CI above 1. The learner loses at 10% budgets and to free-label rules, but those baselines carry an information advantage. So claim 2 is supported with narrowed scope. The ledger has controlled the confound and calls claim 3 dead, so W2 and W3 are false.
